steps.name: agents.expectDmRooms
steps.description: API: a DM room was created per member (the wizard's `dms` step). The room id round-trips through GET /api/matrix/agents.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (with roleIds) to derive member ids.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids.

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectDmRooms
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: agents.expectMembersRunning
steps.description: API: every member exists and is enabled (the orchestrator spawns a container for each enabled member — the UI shows this as the "Active" state). Polled because container spawn + Matrix provisioning settle shortly after `complete`.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (with roleIds) to derive member ids.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids.

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectMembersRunning
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: agents.expectTeamCard
steps.description: UI: the team card and every member row are present on the Agents page. Member ids follow `<teamId>-<roleId>` and are unique text, so we assert on them directly (the team card is expanded by default).

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id shown on the team card.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids (`<teamId>-<roleId>`).

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectTeamCard
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: env.createFixtureEnv
steps.description: Create a Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git-remote fixture repo. Credential-less on purpose: no sshKeyId, no githubTokenId — the orchestrator clones `http://git-remote/…` anonymously and the poller ignores a token-less env, so the team materialises with zero external dependencies.

params.name: id
params.description: Slug id for the new environment.

params.name: name
params.description: Human-readable environment name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at.

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch to track.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.createFixtureEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env
    name: Agentic Demos
    repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"

steps.name: env.deleteEnv
steps.description: Idempotent teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are both success, so a re-run or a partially-failed spec leaves no environment behind.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the environment to delete.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.deleteEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env

steps.name: teardown.deleteEnv
steps.description: Idempotent teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are both success, so a re-run or a partially-failed spec leaves no environment behind.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the environment to delete.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.deleteEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env

steps.name: teardown.teardownTeam
steps.description: A team is a `role: team` agent; deleting it cascades to every member (containers stopped, Matrix users deactivated, volumes/networks torn down) in the orchestrator. Then the now-unreferenced fixture env can be removed.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to delete (cascades to members).

params.name: envId
params.description: Fixture environment id to delete afterwards.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: teardown.teardownTeam
    teamId: agentic-demos
    envId: agentic-demos-env

steps.name: templates.expectTemplateCatalog
steps.description: Assert the template catalog: the New-template action, the ID/Category/Session/ Source columns, and a row for each expected built-in template. Capture point for the template-library screenshot (slide 35 of the walkthrough).

params.name: templateNames
params.description: Built-in template display names each expected as a table row.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: templates.expectTemplateCatalog
    templateNames: [Business Analyst, Developer, Code Reviewer]

steps.name: templates.openTemplatesPage
steps.description: Open the Agent Templates management page and confirm it rendered (its h1).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: templates.openTemplatesPage

steps.name: wizard.createTeamAndExpectProgress
steps.description: Journey-friendly wrapper: submit the wizard and assert the per-step NDJSON progress (plan lists team+members+dms, every step reaches `done`, complete carries the teamId + all members). Encapsulates the F1 inline assertions so a journey can express "create and verify" as a single step-library call. Accepts { teamId, memberIds } or { teamId, roleIds }.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id the complete event must carry.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids (`<teamId>-<roleId>`).

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.createTeamAndExpectProgress
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer, code-reviewer, reworker]

steps.name: wizard.expectEnvironmentStep
steps.description: Assert the Working-Environment step: the named fixture env card (a role=radio) is present and selectable (repo-bearing). Used as the capture point for the env-step screenshot, since selection auto-advances (see selectEnvironment).

params.name: envName
params.description: Visible name of the environment card.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: wizard.expectEnvironmentStep
    envName: Agentic Demos

steps.name: wizard.expectFlowPreview
steps.description: Assert the Process step's live flow preview + wiring check rendered lint-clean (StepProcess.jsx: "Flow preview — N agents" + "Wiring is clean").
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: wizard.expectFlowPreview

steps.name: wizard.expectKnowledgeStep
steps.description: Assert the (optional) Knowledge step rendered — the initial-team-skills picker (capture point for the knowledge-step screenshot).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: wizard.expectKnowledgeStep

steps.name: wizard.expectReviewStep
steps.description: Assert the Review step's summary shows the team identity we are about to create (capture point for the review-step screenshot).

params.name: teamName
params.description: Team display name to expect in the summary.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to expect in the summary.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: wizard.expectReviewStep
    teamName: Agentic Demos
    teamId: agentic-demos

steps.name: wizard.expectTeamIdentity
steps.description: Assert the Team step shows the identity we set (capture point for the screenshot).

params.name: teamName
params.description: Team display name to expect.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to expect.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: wizard.expectTeamIdentity
    teamName: Agentic Demos
    teamId: agentic-demos

steps.name: wizard.next
steps.description: Advance to the next wizard step. Explicit so the runner can screenshot the current step before moving on.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.next

steps.name: wizard.open
steps.description: Open the wizard and confirm the Process step (step 0) is showing.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.open

steps.name: wizard.selectEnvironment
steps.description: Working-Environment step: select the fixture env card (a role=radio). The wizard auto-advances to the Team step on selection, so we wait for the team-name input rather than clicking Next.

params.name: envName
params.description: Visible name of the environment card to select.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.selectEnvironment
    envName: Agentic Demos

steps.name: wizard.selectProcessTemplate
steps.description: Process step: pick a curated template (e.g. "Core SDLC"). Waits for the authoritative lint pass (POST /api/flows/graph) so the bundle is loaded and error-free before the caller advances. Does NOT click Next (see header note).

params.name: templateName
params.description: Visible name of the process template.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.selectProcessTemplate
    templateName: Core SDLC

steps.name: wizard.setTeamIdentity
steps.description: Team step: name + slug id. Filling the id last makes it a manual edit, so the name→slug auto-derivation won't clobber our id. Does NOT advance.

params.name: teamName
params.description: Team display name.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.setTeamIdentity
    teamName: Agentic Demos
    teamId: agentic-demos

steps.name: wizard.skipKnowledge
steps.description: Knowledge step is optional — accept defaults and advance to Review.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.skipKnowledge

steps.name: wizard.submitAndCaptureProgress
steps.description: Review step: submit and capture the NDJSON progress stream the wizard renders. Returns the parsed event list (plan/step/complete) so the spec can assert the per-step progress, and waits for the wizard to consume `complete` (it redirects to the BA chat, or /agents).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: wizard.submitAndCaptureProgress

fixtures.name: teamEnv
fixtures.description: teamEnv: the Team-Setup pilot's precondition. Seeds a credential-less Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git remote, so the wizard can materialise a team with zero external dependencies. Because the journey uses FIXED ids (for screenshot determinism, §7), setup first tears down any leftover team+env from a crashed prior run, and teardown removes the team this journey creates plus the fixture env — one deterministic, idempotent surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id the journey will create (pre-cleaned).

params.name: envId
params.description: Fixture environment id to create.

params.name: envName
params.description: Fixture environment display name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at.

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch to track.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: teamEnv
    params:
      teamId: agentic-demos
      envId: agentic-demos-env
      envName: Agentic Demos
      repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"
